name: Dungmali
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Checked Glottolog dung1252 (refs: only Gerber 2023 subclassification) and Wikipedia Dungmali: no grammar/phonology of Dungmali located; only cognacy note with Bantawa.

sources.citation: Doornenbal, Marius. 2009. A grammar of Bantawa. Utrecht: LOT (held held by the project, catalog bant1281)
sources.note: Mentions Dungmali only as the variety spoken north-east of the Bantawa area; its stress statements concern Bantawa, not Dungmali.

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Mani. 2024. Inclusive-exclusive distinction in the Kirati languages: evidence from Dungmali, Khaling, Koyee, and Wambule. Perspectives on Higher Education 14(1). doi:10.3126/phe.v14i1.76594
sources.note: Nothing; verb/pronoun clusivity morphology only (Dungmali data elicited from a Bhojpur speaker).

sources.citation: Rai, Nirajan. 2019. Making phonemic inventories of Nepali mother tongues and its implications to English language teaching: a case of Dungmali. JODEM: Journal of Language and Literature 10(1): 123-142. doi:10.3126/jodem.v10i1.30405
sources.note: Segmental inventory only: 13 vowel phones (incl. length and nasalisation contrasts), 25 consonants, no contrastive glottal stop; no mention of stress, accent, tone or any suprasegmental. Data drawn from the author's Dungmali Byakaran (grammar, 2015) and dictionary work.

sources.citation: Rai, Tara Mani & Surya Prasad Yadav. 2014 [Wikipedia dates the report 2016]. A sociolinguistic survey of Dungmali: a Tibeto-Burman language. Report submitted to the Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu. ~101 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Chapters cover language use, proficiency, vitality, attitudes, dialect wordlist comparison; Annex D wordlist (5 survey points) is in IPA with no stress marks. Sec. 1.8 'Review of earlier works' (p. 8) names Hansson 1991, Pokharel 1999, Yadava & Turin 2005, a 2005 KRLLC Swadesh list, and Rai 'Batas' 2014 outline as the only earlier works.

sources.citation: Ebert, Karen H. 1991. Inverse and pseudo-inverse prefixes in Kiranti languages: evidence from Belhare, Athpare, and Dungmali. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 14(1): 73-92.
sources.note: Nothing; verb-agreement morphology. States that her Dungmali data come from two LSN verb-morphology questionnaires (no fieldwork), so no phonetic information (scanned with tesseract, scan had no text).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1909. Linguistic Survey of India, vol. III part 1: Tibeto-Burman family: general introduction, specimens of the Tibetan dialects, the Himalayan dialects, and the North Assam group. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Dungmali section pp. 362-363.
sources.note: Nothing; two pages of noun/pronoun/verb notes compiled from Hodgson's vocabularies, no remarks on pronunciation.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid dung1252 and Wikipedia (en, ne) 'Dungmali language'
sources.note: Glottolog lists only Gerber 2023 and ElCat 2022; Wikipedia pages carry no phonology, only the LinSuN survey link and the note that Dungmali is 'largely cognate with Bantawa but differs grammatically and phonologically'.

sources.citation: Rai 'Batas', Nirajan. 2014. [Outline of the Dungmali language, in Nepali; cited as Rai 'Batas' (2014) in Rai & Yadav 2014, p. 8, which gives the dialects Khesange and Dungmali.]
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Named in the LinSuN survey's literature review as the only linguistic outline predating the 2015 grammar.

sources.citation: Rai, Nirajan. 2011. The description of Dungmali: a case of linguistic inclusion and language endangerment. Unpublished research report submitted to the Social Inclusion Research Fund (SIRF), SNV Nepal, Kathmandu.

sources.note: Earliest linguistic description by the grammar's author; SIRF reports sometimes circulate as PDFs but none was located (socialinclusion.org.np unreachable).

sources.citation: Gerber, Pascal. 2023. Vergleich und Rekonstruktion der Oberarun-Sprachen (Kiranti): mit einer Skizze des Westmewahang. PhD dissertation, Universität Bern (pp. 62-68 on Dungmali).
